ai.title: Add publish command to upload agent templates
ai.summary: New `publish` command in `cli/src/commands/publish.ts` uploads local agent templates to backend via POST `/api/agents/publish`. Handles auth check, network errors, and response parsing. Registered in `cli/src/index.tsx` to intercept argv before app init.

eli5.text: You can now share your custom agents from the command line by running the new publish command, which sends your local agent templates to the backend server. Before uploading, the tool checks that you are signed in and handles network errors; if something goes wrong, it tells you a message instead of crashing. This works today: when you run the command, it intercepts the request before the main app starts, uploads your agents over a secure connection, and then exits. If you tried it before this update, that command did not exist.

ai.title: CLI validation errors move from global banner to per-message popover
ai.summary: Validation errors now display in a per-message popover instead of a global banner. This change removes the global banner from `app.tsx` and `chat.tsx`, introducing `validation-error-popover.tsx` and updating `message-block.tsx` to handle local error state. Feedback containers and inputs accept new `errors` and `footerMessage` props to support contextual error reporting. The refactor improves UI clarity by associating validation failures directly with their source messages.

eli5.text: When you type something the program doesn't like, instead of seeing one big error message at the very top or bottom of your screen, you'll now see a small pop-up box attached directly to the message where the problem happened. This makes it clearer which part of what you typed caused the issue, so you can fix it without hunting through a general error list. The program still catches the same mistakes; it just shows them closer to where they occur.

ai.title: Refactor CLI cursor blink logic to remove prop drilling
ai.summary: The `shouldBlinkCursor` prop is removed from `ChatInputBar` and `MultilineInput` call sites in `cli/src/chat.tsx` and `cli/src/components/chat-input-bar.tsx`. `MultilineInput` now derives the blink state directly from `useChatStore` via `isFocusSupported` when the prop is undefined. `FeedbackInputMode` also switches from hardcoded focus to store-driven `inputFocused`. This centralizes cursor visibility logic within the input component and state store.

eli5.text: When you click into the text box to type your message, the blinking cursor now follows a single consistent set of rules instead of being told by multiple different parts of the program. This makes the typing area behave more predictably without you seeing any visible difference, it just keeps working smoothly.

ai.title: Add copy button to message blocks and reduce clipboard delay
ai.summary: New `CopyIconButton` component added to `cli/src/components/copy-icon-button.tsx` and integrated into `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx` footer. Clipboard auto-copy delay in `cli/src/hooks/use-clipboard.ts` reduced from 2000ms to 250ms. Text extraction logic `extractTextFromBlocks` added to `message-block.tsx` to aggregate content from nested blocks.

eli5.text: A small clipboard icon now appears at the bottom of each message in the CLI, letting you copy the full message text to your clipboard with a single click. Hovering over the icon expands it from a small symbol to [⎘ copy], and clicking saves the message exactly as it appears. The assistant also copies messages to the clipboard almost instantly when they arrive, dropping the delay from two seconds to a quarter of a second, so pasted text shows up faster. Both changes are live today.

ai.title: Fix extra closing parenthesis in MessageBlock
ai.summary: Removed an extra closing parenthesis from the MessageBlock component's return statement in cli/src/components/message-block.tsx. This syntax error prevented the component from compiling correctly.

eli5.text: If you use the command-line version of the assistant, you may have seen it fail to start with a cryptic syntax error. The developers removed one stray parenthesis that was breaking the startup sequence, so the assistant's text display component now compiles and renders properly. This fix is live today in the CLI; nothing else about how messages appear changed, but messages will display correctly where they previously would not load at all.

ai.title: Tool params rename and WebSocket schema removal
ai.summary: Renamed $toolParams to toolParams and parameters to inputSchema across tool definitions. Removed CLIENT_MESSAGE_SCHEMA validation from WebSocket server. Updated add_message tool with new description format.

eli5.text: The system has renamed a couple of internal labels it uses to describe tools (like the assistant's search or coding helpers) so they follow a more standard naming convention, which makes the tool descriptions show up more consistently and clearly. It also removed a validation step on the server that was checking incoming messages before processing them, meaning messages are now accepted and handled without that extra filtering layer. If you use the agent, you'd notice tool call descriptions reading more predictably, and the backend processes WebSocket messages with one less validation hurdle. These changes are live and take effect immediately for anyone interacting with the agent runtime over a WebSocket connection today.

ai.title: Move sendSubagentChunk from state to params
ai.summary: Refactor `sendSubagentChunk` from `State` object to `CodebuffToolHandlerFunction` params in `handler-function-type.ts`. Updates `spawn-agents.ts` to consume it from params, removing internal state checks. Modifies `stream-parser.ts` and `tool-executor.ts` to stop passing it via state.

eli5.text: When the system needs to send small pieces of progress from a helper agent up to the main assistant, it now passes that capability in directly instead of tucking it away in a shared storage box. You can see the difference in how the agent-spawning code receives and uses this messaging hook, since it no longer checks the shared box for it. Everything works the same from your end today, but this makes the data flow easier to follow if you're tracing how a sub-agent streams its reply back.

ai.title: Remove agentState from tool execution state
ai.summary: Removed agentState from the internal State object in packages/agent-runtime. Tools now receive agentState directly via handler parameters instead of accessing it through state. This change affects set-output, spawn-agent-inline, and spawn-agents handlers, plus stream-parser and tool-executor.

eli5.text: When you use tools that spawn sub-agents or set outputs, the system no longer carries your agent state through a shared internal container. Instead, it passes your agent state directly to each tool handler when it runs, so tools access it as a direct parameter rather than reaching through a state object. You won't notice anything different while using the product today, but this is a behind-the-scenes cleanup that makes the code more organized and removes an extra layer of indirection. The change is already live and affects only the internal wiring, not any visible behavior.

ai.title: Remove fullResponse from agent runtime state
ai.summary: Removed `fullResponse` from `State` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/handler-function-type.ts` and `write-file.ts`. Updated `stream-parser.ts` to use local `fullResponse` variable instead of passing it through state. This cleanup reduces state complexity in the agent runtime.

eli5.text: The agent's internal state was carrying a piece of text (fullResponse) that it didn't actually need, so developers removed it from where it was stored and instead kept it as a simple local variable that only the part of the code reading the response actually uses. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup in the agent runtime: there's no new feature or behavior for users, just less clutter in how the agent's conversation state is organized. The change is live today but only affects how the code is structured, not what you see or do.

ai.title: Refactor agent state to remove system prompt dependency
ai.summary: Removes the `system` property from the shared `State` type in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/handler-function-type.ts`, moving it to explicit parameters in tool handlers like `spawn-agent-inline.ts` and `spawn-agents.ts`. This decouples system prompt handling from the generic state object, requiring handlers to receive `system` directly via function arguments rather than extracting it from `state`. The change affects `run-programmatic-step.ts` initialization logic, where `state` construction no longer includes `system`, and updates `validateSpawnState` in `spawn-agent-utils.ts` to stop validating for `system`. Tests in `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/` reflect these structural changes to state passing.

eli5.text: The assistant's instruction manual is no longer being stuffed inside a shared pocket that every tool reaches into; instead, each tool now receives the instruction manual directly as its own parameter when it is called. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup that changes how the assistant pieces are connected internally, without altering what you see or how the assistant behaves when you interact with it. Engineers working on the assistant will need to pass the instruction manual explicitly in fewer places now, but everyday users will not notice any difference in performance or features.
